Business Context / Rule: Supports documentation, distribution, accounting, and identification across societies.

Business Definition: Alternate Writer identity classified as Professional Name, Translated Name, Romanized Name, Matching Name, Statement Name, Alternate Name, or Legal Name, optionally with its own IPI/CAE Name Number.
Business Context / Rule: Use for searching, matching, statementing, legal-name identification, professional attribution, transliteration, translation, and external rights identification.

Business Definition: Association of a Writer or Publisher with a society for a specified right type.
Business Context / Rule: Use the right-specific society field.

Business Definition: A recording-level entity ingested into the Tempo chart process from external chart or consumption data. A Chart Song is described by source title, artist, ISRC, and source identifiers and may be associated with a Tempo Song representing the underlying musical work. One Tempo Song can potentially relate to multiple recordings, so Chart Song and Tempo Song must not be treated as interchangeable.
Business Context / Rule: Use Chart Song as the recording-level entity for chart, radio, sales, and streaming activity. Do not join or aggregate solely by title or artist. Use chart_song_id for the recording and tempo_song_id for the matched musical work.

Business Definition: A Chart Song that has been associated with a Tempo Song through the chart-matching workflow. The association supports identification of SMP-controlled repertoire and connects market activity to the underlying musical work. Match Status and the confirmation, control, association, and pending indicators should be retained when evaluating the reliability and business readiness of the match.
Business Context / Rule: Use for income-tracking and revenue-assurance analysis only when the match workflow context is preserved. A populated Tempo Song ID does not independently prove that the match is confirmed or that SMP controls the work.

Business Definition: A Chart Song represented as Pending Song in the matching workflow because the recording or its Writer/control information is not yet complete enough for final association. Pending records may contain provisional Writer information and legacy control-percentage fields.
Business Context / Rule: Treat as work in progress. Use pending Writer and total-control fields for investigation, not as certified repertoire ownership. Pending records should remain distinguishable from Possible Match and Unmatched records.

Business Definition: The chart-song identifier intended to represent the primary or canonical record when duplicate or related Chart Song records exist. It can support consolidated analysis, but the exact hierarchy, deduplication rules, and cardinality remain subject to SME confirmation.
Business Context / Rule: Use only as a candidate canonical identifier until PD-0802 confirms hierarchy and deduplication rules. Retain chart_song_id in detail reporting so related recording records remain traceable.

Business Definition: Governed classification of a Chart Song within the Tempo matching workflow. Valid statuses are Match, Possible Match, Pending Song, Not Controlled, Unknown, and Unmatched. Use the status with match confirmation, control, pending, association, and active indicators when deciding whether the record is ready for reporting or follow-up.
Business Context / Rule: Always interpret with match_confirmed_indicator, controlled_indicator, pending_song_ind, song_association_indicator, initial_automatch_indicator, and active_indicator. The status determines workflow state, not necessarily ownership or revenue outcome.

Business Definition: Chart Match Status indicating that the Chart Song is matched to a Tempo Song. This status identifies an association but should still be interpreted with the confirmation and control indicators for workflow and reporting purposes.
Business Context / Rule: A Match indicates an association to a Tempo Song. Before using the row as certified matched repertoire, also evaluate confirmation, control, and active indicators.

Business Definition: Chart Match Status indicating that a candidate Tempo Song association has been identified but requires additional verification before being treated as a confirmed match.
Business Context / Rule: Exclude from confirmed-match KPIs unless explicitly analyzing the review queue. Possible Match records require verification before being used for controlled-repertoire reporting.

Business Definition: Chart Match Status indicating that the Chart Song requires additional Song, Writer, or control information before the matching workflow can be completed.
Business Context / Rule: Use for records requiring Song, Writer, or control completion. Pending Song records can carry provisional control percentages and Writer information but should not be treated as final ownership data.

Business Definition: Chart Match Status indicating that the recording or associated musical work is not considered controlled by SMP for the chart-matching purpose.
Business Context / Rule: Exclude from SMP-controlled opportunity totals unless the analysis is specifically reviewing negative control determinations. Retain for auditability and to prevent repeated matching work.

Business Definition: Chart Match Status used when the match or control outcome is not known. Treat separately from Unmatched because Unknown does not necessarily mean that matching activity was completed without a result.
Business Context / Rule: Keep separate from Unmatched. Unknown indicates insufficient or unresolved status information, while Unmatched represents a defined workflow outcome.

Business Definition: Chart Match Status indicating that the Chart Song is not associated with a Tempo Song. Unmatched records are candidates for matching review and revenue-assurance investigation when market activity suggests potential SMP repertoire.
Business Context / Rule: Use as a candidate population for repertoire-matching and revenue-assurance review. Chart activity on an Unmatched record is a signal for investigation, not proof that SMP controls the work.

Business Definition: A Chart Song association initially produced through an automated matching process rather than solely through manual review. The initial automatch indicator describes match origin and does not by itself prove that the match was confirmed or controlled.
Business Context / Rule: Use to identify match origin and support automation-quality monitoring. Automated Match does not replace confirmation or control validation.

Business Definition: A proposed Chart Song-to-Tempo Song association that has been confirmed in the matching workflow. Confirmation should be evaluated separately from whether SMP controls the associated work.
Business Context / Rule: Use as the confirmation component of matched-repertoire reporting. Confirmation does not establish SMP control by itself; use the controlled status separately.

Business Definition: A Chart Song whose matched musical work is classified as controlled by SMP for chart-matching purposes. Control status supports prioritization of market activity for income tracking and revenue assurance.
Business Context / Rule: Use to prioritize market activity associated with SMP-controlled repertoire. Preserve the match and confirmation states because control and match quality are separate business dimensions.

Business Definition: Combined SMP-controlled share exposed for a pending Chart Song by adding the legacy Sony/SATV, EMI, and 50/50 control-percentage columns and treating null components as zero. The three components reflect a historical entity structure that is no longer current; business users should rely on the combined total rather than interpreting the individual columns as current entity allocations.
Business Context / Rule: For pending songs, calculate the combined total from all three legacy component columns with nulls treated as zero. Use the combined total for current SMP reporting. Flag values above 100% for review because 100% is the expected theoretical maximum, although database enforcement is not confirmed.

Business Definition: Legacy column originally intended to store the Sony/SATV-controlled percentage of a pending Song. Following consolidation into SMP, the SMP total may be placed in this or another legacy component column, so the field should not be used as a current legal-entity allocation.
Business Context / Rule: Do not report this column as a current SATV/Sony legal-entity allocation. It is a legacy storage field and may contain the full consolidated SMP percentage.

Business Definition: Legacy column originally intended to store the EMI-controlled percentage of a pending Song. Following consolidation into SMP, the SMP total may be placed in this or another legacy component column, so the field should not be used as a current legal-entity allocation.
Business Context / Rule: Do not report this column as a current EMI legal-entity allocation. It is a legacy storage field and may contain the full consolidated SMP percentage.

Business Definition: Legacy column originally intended to store the percentage controlled through the historical 50/50 entity. Following consolidation into SMP, the SMP total may be placed in this or another legacy component column, so the field should not be used as a current legal-entity allocation.
Business Context / Rule: Do not report this column as a current 50/50 legal-entity allocation. It is a legacy storage field and may contain the full consolidated SMP percentage.

Business Definition: A source-file ingestion event that loads chart observations into Tempo. The upload is identified by Chart Upload Header ID and described by file name, file type, country, creator, and creation timestamp. Retain this context for traceability, reconciliation, and investigation of source corrections.
Business Context / Rule: Retain Chart Upload Header ID in reconciliation and source-quality analysis. Records from different files or reloads must not be assumed to be distinct business activity without understanding restatement rules.

Business Definition: Chart File Type identifies the source chart feed, provider, or ingestion format responsible for the uploaded chart activity. Different file types may use different methodologies, populations, territories, ranking rules, and measurement techniques and should not automatically be considered directly comparable.
Business Context / Rule: Use Chart File Type to distinguish feed structures and processing expectations.

Business Definition: Chart Type identifies the chart methodology, audience, genre, format, ranking process, or reporting category associated with a chart observation. Chart measures should generally only be compared or aggregated within compatible Chart Types because ranking criteria, source feeds, provider coverage, market definitions, and measurement methodologies can differ substantially between chart categories.
Business Context / Rule: Retain Chart Type when comparing rank, chart tenure, and sales. Valid rank ranges and business populations can differ by chart type.

Business Definition: Ordinal placement of a Song or Album on a named chart for a reporting week. Lower numeric values generally represent stronger placement. Rank is not additive and should not be summed; comparisons should remain within the same chart, geography, and period definition.
Business Context / Rule: Rank is ordinal, not additive. Do not sum ranks. Compare ranks only within compatible chart type, chart name, geography, and period contexts; lower values generally indicate better placement.

Business Definition: A monitored radio-play detection reported for a Chart Song during the quarterly observation. Detects are additive only when station, market, song, upload, and period overlap have been accounted for.
Business Context / Rule: Sum only across non-overlapping observation populations. Preserve Chart Song, upload, country, and quarter context and apply the approved source-deduplication methodology when available.

Business Definition: Estimated audience exposure associated with radio detections for a Chart Song during a quarterly period. Audience is an exposure estimate and may overlap across stations or markets, so it should not be summed without an approved aggregation methodology.
Business Context / Rule: Do not sum audience across overlapping stations, markets, or reporting populations without an approved methodology. Treat audience as estimated exposure rather than a count of unique people.

Business Definition: Streams initiated on demand and reported through overall, audio, premium-audio, advertising-supported audio, and video measures. Component measures may overlap with broader totals, so reconciliation rules must be confirmed before combining them.
Business Context / Rule: Do not add overall streams to component stream measures. Confirm whether audio, premium, ad-supported, and video categories are mutually exclusive or hierarchical before reconciliation.

Business Definition: Audio streams delivered through programmed or curated playback rather than captured in the source on-demand audio categories. The exact interactivity and overlap rules require confirmation before combining with other stream measures.
Business Context / Rule: Keep separate from on-demand measures until the source confirms interactivity and overlap rules. Do not assume programmed streams are a component of overall on-demand streams.

Business Definition: Number of streams reported for a Chart Song for a specific Digital Service Provider, Service Tier, Calculation Model, and week-ending date. Aggregate only when those dimensions represent non-overlapping activity.
Business Context / Rule: Aggregate only across non-overlapping Digital Service Provider, Service Tier, Calculation Model, Chart Song, and week dimensions. Preserve provider/tier/model for reconciliation.

Business Definition: Service or platform associated with a weekly streaming observation. Retain the provider dimension when aggregating because the same Chart Song can have activity across multiple providers.
Business Context / Rule: Retain provider in all stream aggregations unless cross-provider activity is intentionally summed. Provider names are descriptive and should not substitute for a governed provider key where one exists.

Business Definition: Commercial or access tier associated with a streaming observation. The field enables analysis by tier but should not be interpreted until the governed values and overlap rules are documented.
Business Context / Rule: Use as a segmentation dimension only after valid values and overlap rules are approved. Do not assume tiers are mutually exclusive or directly comparable across providers.

Business Definition: Source-defined model used to classify or calculate a weekly streaming observation. Retain the model when aggregating and comparing measures because different models may not be directly additive or comparable.
Business Context / Rule: Retain the model when comparing or aggregating streams. Measures produced under different calculation models may not be directly comparable or additive.

Business Definition: Business process of using matched repertoire and consumption or chart activity to identify, monitor, and investigate income opportunities associated with SMP-controlled works. In SA-008, matched chart recordings and market-performance observations provide evidence for prioritizing follow-up.
Business Context / Rule: Use chart and consumption activity to prioritize investigation of potential income related to SMP-controlled repertoire. The activity is evidence for review, not a booked receivable or confirmed royalty.

Business Definition: Business discipline of using controls, reconciliation, and analysis to identify activity that may not be fully captured in downstream revenue processes and to reduce potential revenue leakage. In SA-008, matching chart recordings to Tempo repertoire helps surface controlled activity for investigation; the chart data itself does not prove that revenue is due or missing.
Business Context / Rule: Use matched chart activity as a control and investigation input to identify potential revenue leakage or incomplete processing. Do not infer an underpayment solely from chart presence, rank, audience, sales, or streams.

Business Definition: Process of associating an externally reported recording with the appropriate Tempo Song so SMP control can be evaluated and market activity can be connected to the underlying musical work. Matching may be automated, possible, pending, confirmed, unmatched, unknown, or not controlled according to the workflow.
Business Context / Rule: Preserve source recording identifiers, match status, confirmation, control, and Tempo Song association so each match remains explainable and auditable. Recording-to-work matching should not collapse distinct recordings.

Business Definition: Chart, radio, sales, or streaming activity linked to a potentially controlled Song and used to prioritize income-tracking or revenue-assurance review. A signal indicates activity requiring analysis; it is not, by itself, evidence of a royalty underpayment or revenue loss.
Business Context / Rule: Use as a prioritization indicator for investigation. A signal must not be presented as confirmed revenue, loss, royalty entitlement, or financial exposure without downstream validation.

Business Definition: A commercial release, album, compilation, physical product, digital product, or other product configuration for which mechanical licensing information is maintained in Tempo.
Business Context / Rule: A Mechanical Product is the parent licensing entity for one or more Mechanical Product Song records. Product-level amounts, quantities, percentages, identifiers, licensing dates, and License-to-Date measures must be interpreted at product grain and should not be combined with song-level values unless overlap has been assessed.

Business Definition: A current song-level licensing record representing a song or track included on a Mechanical Product.
Business Context / Rule: Each record belongs to a Mechanical Product and can carry song-specific rates, percentages, advances, workflow dates, track attributes, matching indicators, and notes. mechanical_product_song_id must be populated but is not independently unique, so it must not be used alone to deduplicate rows.

Business Definition: An authorization governing the reproduction and distribution of a musical composition in connection with a product or recording configuration.
Business Context / Rule: SA-009 documents mechanical licensing operations separately from Sync Licensing. Interpret License Number, Tempo License ID, License Type, License Status, workflow dates, rates, percentages, and product/song context together.

Business Definition: The authoritative Tempo identifier for a Mechanical Product.
Business Context / Rule: The value must be populated and unique in mechanical_product_v. It is the parent relationship key used by mechanical_product_song_v and should be used for product-level joins and counts.

Business Definition: Identifier assigned to a Mechanical Product Song record.
Business Context / Rule: The value must be populated but is not required to be unique. A broader composite grain is required for deduplication and remains subject to validation.

Business Definition: The party receiving or operating under the mechanical licensing rights represented by the product.
Business Context / Rule: Use Licensee ID for joins and Licensee Name for business reporting. Licensee enrichment is optional because the supplied views use LEFT JOINs.

Business Definition: Governed classification describing the category of license represented by the product.
Business Context / Rule: SA-009 reuses the License Type domain already documented for SA-006. Use the governed name rather than interpreting the numeric identifier without its reference value.

Business Definition: The current lifecycle or processing status assigned to a Mechanical Product license.
Business Context / Rule: The allowed values and workflow transitions have not yet been supplied. Do not create status groupings or infer completion until the governed domain is documented.

Business Definition: Mechanical license reference associated with a product or product-song record.
Business Context / Rule: Use with Tempo License ID and Mechanical Product Release ID. The distinctions, uniqueness, and cross-system roles of these identifiers require SME confirmation.

Business Definition: Tempo system identifier associated with a Mechanical Product license.
Business Context / Rule: Do not assume this identifier is interchangeable with License Number or Mechanical Product Release ID until their relationship is validated.

Business Definition: Business or operational product identifier used in mechanical licensing.
Business Context / Rule: A product can also expose a Primary Product Number. The precedence and relationship between these identifiers require validation; neither should be assumed unique without evidence.

Business Definition: External commercial identifier associated with a product or release.
Business Context / Rule: Use for product matching and reconciliation. The field can represent UPC or EAN; format, population, and uniqueness rules require validation before use as a key.

Business Definition: Artist information recorded at Mechanical Product grain.
Business Context / Rule: Product Artist can differ from Song Artist for compilations, featured performances, or products containing multiple artists. Do not overwrite or substitute one for the other.

Business Definition: Artist information recorded for the specific song occurrence on a Mechanical Product.
Business Context / Rule: Interpret at product-song grain and compare with Product Artist when distinguishing release-level and track-level artist information.

Business Definition: International Standard Recording Code stored for a product-song recording.
Business Context / Rule: ISRC identifies a recording rather than the underlying composition. Use with Song ID, Song Sequence ID, product, and track context; format and uniqueness controls remain to be confirmed.

Business Definition: Tracking reference associated with HFA mechanical licensing activity.
Business Context / Rule: Use for operational reconciliation of product-song licensing. Issuing workflow, format, and uniqueness rules require Mechanical Licensing SME confirmation.

Business Definition: Rate used as a basis for mechanical licensing calculations for a product-song record.
Business Context / Rule: Interpret Rate Amount with Licensing Rate Type, Reduction Rate, duration, units, Currency Code, Controlled Percentage, and Collectable Percentage. The stored calculation basis requires validation.

Business Definition: Governed classification describing how a product-song mechanical rate is determined or applied.
Business Context / Rule: The domain values and calculation behavior have not yet been supplied. Use the resolved Rate Type Name and do not compare rates across types without confirmed methodology.

Business Definition: Percentage adjustment applied to the applicable mechanical licensing rate or payable basis.
Business Context / Rule: The calculation order, valid range, and interaction with Base Rate, Controlled Rate, and Collectable Rate require SME validation.

Business Definition: Percentage of the represented song interest controlled by SMP for the applicable mechanical licensing record.
Business Context / Rule: Product-level and product-song-level controlled percentages are stored at different grains. Do not sum percentages across songs or products without confirmed weighting and roll-up rules.

Business Definition: Percentage of the represented song interest that SMP is entitled or configured to collect under the licensing arrangement.
Business Context / Rule: Collectable Percentage may differ from Controlled Percentage. Product totals should not be recreated by simply summing product-song percentages unless the approved weighting logic is known.

Business Definition: Rate amount attributable to the controlled portion of the product-song record.
Business Context / Rule: The formula connecting Rate Amount, Controlled Percentage, Reduction Rate, and other terms is not exposed by the view and requires validation.

Business Definition: Rate amount attributable to the collectable portion of the product-song record.
Business Context / Rule: The formula connecting the base rate, controlled and collectable percentages, reductions, and licensing terms requires validation.

Business Definition: Amount paid or recorded in advance under the mechanical licensing arrangement.
Business Context / Rule: Interpret Advance Amount in Currency Code and at the documented product or product-song grain. Product-level and song-level advances may overlap and should not be combined until allocation rules are confirmed.

Business Definition: Quantity of units associated with the mechanical advance terms.
Business Context / Rule: Use with Advance Amount and the applicable product or product-song grain. Confirm whether the units represent a threshold, prepaid quantity, or another contractual basis.

Business Definition: Quantity of Mechanical Product units reported as sold.
Business Context / Rule: Use Units Sold As-of Date to determine the reporting point. Confirm whether the value is period activity or a cumulative snapshot before aggregation.

Business Definition: Stored estimate of the amount expected to be collectable for a Mechanical Product.
Business Context / Rule: The view does not expose the calculation. Confirm whether the estimate is gross or net and how units, rates, controlled share, collectable share, advances, and currency affect the amount.

Business Definition: Product-level indication that income has been matched to a Mechanical Product.
Business Context / Rule: The valid values and matching workflow require confirmation. Keep separate from Income Matched to Product and Matched to Statement Line until the relationship among these fields is validated.

Business Definition: Product-song-level indication that income has been associated with the parent Mechanical Product.
Business Context / Rule: The valid values, matching process, and distinction from product-level Income Matched require validation before use in reconciliation metrics.

Business Definition: Product-song-level indication that the licensing record has been matched to a royalty Statement Line.
Business Context / Rule: The field is presumed to reference Statement Line matching based on its name, but the values, matching grain, and downstream income effect require SME confirmation.

Business Definition: Date on which the mechanical licensing request was initiated or recorded.
Business Context / Rule: Use with Received Date and Issued Date for workflow analysis. The exact initiating event requires confirmation before calculating turnaround times.

Business Definition: Date on which licensing documentation, approval, or a response was received.
Business Context / Rule: The precise received event and responsible party require confirmation. Do not assume the date means payment receipt or income receipt.

Business Definition: Date on which the mechanical license was issued.
Business Context / Rule: Represents a licensing workflow milestone and should not be substituted for Product Release Date or File Upload Date.

Business Definition: Date when income from the Mechanical Product is expected to begin.
Business Context / Rule: This is an expected or planning date, not evidence of actual income receipt. Use for monitoring and forecasting only after the business process is confirmed.

Business Definition: Measures accumulated or assessed from the beginning of the applicable license through the current reporting point.
Business Context / Rule: For SA-009, LTD means License to Date, not Life to Date. License-to-Date quantities and percentages are cumulative or as-of measures and should not be summed across successive reporting points for the same product.

Business Definition: Cumulative product units sold through the License-to-Date reporting point.
Business Context / Rule: Treat as a snapshot and use the related License-to-Date Units Sold Date. The exact event represented by that date remains subject to validation.

Business Definition: Stored License-to-Date total Song AGC value for a Mechanical Product.
Business Context / Rule: AGC expansion, unit, and calculation methodology have not been supplied. Do not interpret or aggregate this measure until validated.

Business Definition: Stored License-to-Date total pro rata mechanical rate for a Mechanical Product.
Business Context / Rule: Calculation methodology, currency or unit, and weighting across songs require validation. Rates are not additive without confirmed logic.

Business Definition: Stored License-to-Date percentage classified as set to pay.
Business Context / Rule: The numerator, denominator, process stage, and valid range require validation before operational or KPI use.

Business Definition: Stored License-to-Date percentage classified as licensed for the Mechanical Product.
Business Context / Rule: Eligibility, denominator, and relationship to Controlled and Collectable Percentage require validation.

Business Definition: Number of occurrences of a song or recording on a Mechanical Product.
Business Context / Rule: Confirm treatment of repeated tracks, medleys, alternate versions, hidden tracks, and bonus tracks before using the value to count distinct songs.

Business Definition: Song occurrence designated as supplemental content beyond the standard product configuration.
Business Context / Rule: Confirm whether Bonus Track status affects licensed percentage, rates, advances, track counts, or reporting eligibility.

Business Definition: Song occurrence intentionally not shown in the standard visible track listing.
Business Context / Rule: Confirm whether Hidden Track status affects licensing treatment, units, rate calculations, or product track counts.

Business Definition: Product-song record classified as a single.
Business Context / Rule: Confirm whether the indicator describes the track, the product release, or a licensing-rate treatment, as well as allowed values and null handling.

Business Definition: Contractual condition intended to provide licensing treatment no less favorable than the treatment afforded to comparable parties or works.
Business Context / Rule: Represented by favorite_nation_ind. Exact contractual scope, allowed values, and consequences for rate calculations require legal or Mechanical Licensing SME validation.

Business Definition: Indicator related to tracking or matching income for a Mechanical Product or Mechanical Product Song.
Business Context / Rule: The product-level and song-level fields may serve different purposes. Their valid values and effect on income matching require validation.

Business Definition: Upload notes transformed into readable text by removing HTML tags, excess spaces, selected escaped punctuation, and encoding artifacts.
Business Context / Rule: Use as unstructured operational context. The transformation improves readability but does not convert notes into a governed classification or status.

Business Definition: A curated summary of royalty earnings from the Client perspective with Song-level detail and office-currency measures.
Business Context / Rule: Use for approved Client/Song earnings analysis across historical and current periods. Grain includes more dimensions than Client and Song; users must retain required dimensions when re-aggregating.

Business Definition: Currency of the office from which the Client originates and in which this view stores its monetary measures.
Business Context / Rule: Currency is a mandatory grouping dimension for financial analysis. Do not sum across originating offices/currencies without approved conversion.

Business Definition: Amount posted to the General Ledger, summarized from GL Posting Amount.
Business Context / Rule: Normally Royalty Payable plus NPS; zero for Participant Rate Type. Aggregate only within a common currency.

Business Definition: Amount payable to the Client in this Client-perspective summary.
Business Context / Rule: Although the source field can represent intercompany pass-through in other contexts, here it always represents the Client payable.

Business Definition: Final NPS earned by the Client Originating Office.
Business Context / Rule: Excludes NPS retained by the original processing office and must not be interpreted as total SMP NPS.

Business Definition: Reporting rule that shifts source hierarchy one level right for affiliate/intercompany earnings.
Business Context / Rule: Example: UK receipt PRS > BBC Radio becomes SMP UK > PRS > BBC Radio after intercompany processing.

Business Definition: High-level reporting rollup of earnings into Mech, Perf, Sync, and Other.
Business Context / Rule: Mechanical and Digital Mechanical roll to Mech; Performance and Digital Performance to Perf; users may choose this or the more detailed Income Type Group based on analytical need.

Business Definition: Governed lower-level Tempo grouping for Income Types.
Business Context / Rule: Provides greater granularity than Income Group, including Digital Mechanical versus Mechanical and Digital Performance versus Performance.

Business Definition: Classification derived from the governed streaming flag on the detailed Income Type.
Business Context / Rule: Use with either Income Group or Income Type Group to distinguish Streaming from Non-Streaming earnings.

Business Definition: Business reporting classification that divides relevant royalties into US, Disco, SMP Global, or standard office name.
Business Context / Rule: Not an enterprise-governed reference domain; embedded in the view to support US Finance reporting.

Business Definition: US Finance reporting category for US Latin repertoire.
Business Context / Rule: Clients linked to company groups DISC, DINT, LATU, 50D, and SMD, plus processing office 169, are classified as Disco under the view logic.

Business Definition: Tempo processing-office/reporting category for global digital deals signed from the US and covering multiple territories.
Business Context / Rule: Distinguishes multi-territory US-signed agreements from true US royalty sources.

Business Definition: Transaction category for Client earnings received by foreign affiliates.
Business Context / Rule: Derived for transaction types 75/77 with GL Mapping Type 2.

Business Definition: Transaction category for earnings received in the same country in which the Client is signed.
Business Context / Rule: Default external category when the IntraGroup and External Foreign Deal conditions do not apply.

Business Definition: Internal financial-reporting rollup used for advances, recoupment, write-offs, and deal financial analysis.
Business Context / Rule: Does not affect Client Statements. Maintained by the US Deal Modeling team and owned by Tom Foley.

Business Definition: Royalty-settlement rollup Client receiving consolidated transactions and determining ultimate payable and Client-facing statement position.
Business Context / Rule: Defaults to the Client when no cross-to Client relationship is populated.

Business Definition: Rule combining a fixed historical summary with current Earnings Lines.
Business Context / Rule: Current branch is accounting periods after 01-Apr-2024; historical branch comes from monthend_rate_analysis_song_hist_mv. Populations are mutually exclusive and combined with UNION ALL.

Business Definition: Normalized half-year endpoint derived from Statement Date.
Business Context / Rule: January-June maps to 30-Jun; July-December maps to 31-Dec.

Business Definition: The accounting period assigned to a royalty transaction for financial recognition, royalty processing, reporting, and ledger posting purposes. The Accounting Period determines when earnings are recognized within Tempo and serves as the primary period used for royalty accounting, financial reporting, accruals, and earnings analysis.
Business Context / Rule: The Accounting Period is not necessarily the same as the royalty source reporting period, usage period, payment period, or statement period. Multiple royalty transactions originating from different sources may be recognized within the same Accounting Period. Accounting Period is frequently used as the primary reporting period for earnings, accrual, and revenue-analysis reporting and is the basis for fiscal and calendar period derivations used throughout financial reporting. In SA‑010, the Accounting Period is also used to partition historical and current earnings populations and to derive Fiscal Period reporting attributes.

Business Definition: The reporting period used to group royalty transactions into a single Client royalty statement cycle. Statement Period Date represents the royalty reporting period under which earnings will be included on a Client royalty statement and associated royalty payment generated by SMP.
Business Context / Rule: Statement Period Date reflects the royalty-statement period from the Client perspective rather than the external source reporting period. It is used to group royalty transactions that will appear together on the same Client statement and payment cycle. Depending on the Client's deal terms and reporting frequency, Statement Periods commonly align to semiannual or quarterly royalty reporting cycles. Statement Period Date may differ from Accounting Period Date because royalty transactions can be recognized in one Accounting Period while still belonging to a different Client Statement Period. Statement Period Date is a key reporting dimension used for Client statement preparation, statement reconciliation, royalty payment forecasting, and royalty-distribution reporting. In SA‑010, Statement Period Date is also used to derive the Semiannual Statement Date reporting dimension.

Business Definition: Client Financials represents the royalty information presented within the Tempo Client module Financial tab. It provides a Client-focused view of calculated royalty receipts after Song matching, royalty calculation, and the Tempo Earnings Line Summarization process have completed.
Business Context / Rule: Use Client Financials to reproduce and explain amounts displayed in the Tempo Client Financials screen. Reporting is organized by Statement Period rather than Accounting Period. Each row represents a calculated Client royalty receipt for a Statement Period, includes Song-level royalties and the maximum Source and Sub Source detail available in Tempo, and presents monetary amounts in the Client Originating Office currency. The view is intended for operational Client royalty analysis and UI reconciliation rather than transaction-level Earnings Line investigation.

Business Definition: A Tempo processing step executed after royalty calculations complete that aggregates detailed Earnings Line activity into performance-optimized structures used by the Tempo user interface and downstream operational reporting views.
Business Context / Rule: The process creates summarized structures such as tempo_song_stmnt_orig_sub_sub_summ so Tempo can return commonly requested royalty information without aggregating raw Earnings Lines at query time. Client Financials consumes this post-calculation summary layer. Users should therefore interpret its rows as summarized calculated royalty receipts, not individual incoming statement lines or individual Earnings Lines.

Business Definition: A royalty amount attributed to a Client after an incoming royalty transaction has matched to a Song and completed the royalty-calculation process.
Business Context / Rule: This is the business event represented by a Client Financials row. The receipt is reported for a Client Statement Period, includes Song-level detail, and retains the greatest Source hierarchy detail available. Multiple calculated receipts may exist for the same Client and Statement Period because Contract, Subcontract, Song, Source, Income Type, Rate Type, Transaction Type, Company, and other processing attributes can differ.

Business Definition: The reporting period used to group royalty transactions into a single Client royalty statement cycle and associated royalty payment distribution.
Business Context / Rule: Statement Period Date reflects when royalty earnings are expected to be reported to and paid to the Client. Depending on contractual terms, Client statements may follow quarterly, semiannual, or other cycles. It is not the same as Accounting Period Date: Accounting Period identifies when SMP recognizes or processes the royalty, while Statement Period identifies the Client-facing statement and payment cycle. Client Financials exposes Statement Period Date and does not expose Accounting Period Date.

Business Definition: The currency of the office from which the Client originates and the currency in which Client Financials monetary measures are presented.
Business Context / Rule: All monetary amounts in Client Financials must be interpreted together with currency_cd. Users must not sum values across Clients originating from offices with different currencies unless an approved currency-conversion method is applied. Include currency_cd in aggregations, reconciliations, exports, and visualizations to prevent mixed-currency totals.

Business Definition: The calculated gross royalty amount attributed to a Client after the incoming statement line has matched to a Song and completed royalty calculation, but before withholding-tax and NPS calculations are applied.
Business Context / Rule: Gross Client Income is a post-calculation value and must not be interpreted as the raw amount received on an incoming statement line. It is an early Client-perspective amount in the royalty distribution flow and provides the starting point for understanding subsequent tax, NPS, payable, local-income, and net-income treatments. Aggregate only within a common Client Originating Office currency.

Business Definition: A Client Financials monetary measure sourced from the Tempo Earnings Line Summarization layer and presented in the Client Originating Office currency.
Business Context / Rule: The authoritative business definition and its calculation relationship to Gross Client Income, Client Net Income, withholding tax, NPS, and Royalty Payable have not yet been confirmed. Until validation is complete, users may reproduce the value shown in Tempo but should not infer a formula or use the measure as a certified enterprise KPI. Tracked under PV-SEL-031.

Business Definition: A Client Financials monetary measure representing a downstream Client income amount calculated by Tempo and presented in the Client Originating Office currency.
Business Context / Rule: The authoritative business definition and the deductions or adjustments included in Client Net Income have not yet been confirmed. Users should not assume it equals Gross Client Income less withholding tax, NPS, or any particular combination of measures. It may be used to reproduce Tempo UI results, but should not be promoted as a certified KPI until PV-SEL-032 is resolved.

Business Definition: The royalty amount payable to the Client for the calculated royalty receipt.
Business Context / Rule: Within Client Financials, Royalty Payable is interpreted from the Client perspective. It is presented in the Client Originating Office currency and should be aggregated only with currency_cd or after approved conversion. The value supports Client payment review and statement reconciliation, but it should not be assumed to equal Gross, Local, or Net Client Income without a validated calculation relationship.

Business Definition: The actual withholding tax deducted from the Client’s royalty earnings based on where the Client is based and which SMP affiliate collected or processed the royalty.
Business Context / Rule: This is a realized tax deduction rather than an estimate or accrual. The amount can vary according to Client location, collecting affiliate, applicable local tax requirements, and relevant treaty treatment. It directly affects the Client’s royalty outcome and is commonly used for Client payment review, tax reconciliation, and explanation of differences between gross and downstream royalty amounts.

Business Definition: The final NPS earned by the Client Originating Office for the calculated royalty receipt.
Business Context / Rule: Client Office NPS does not represent total NPS earned by SMP. If a collecting or original processing affiliate retains NPS before intercompany remittance, that retained amount is excluded from nps_am and may be represented as Foreign NPS. Use Client Office NPS to analyze the NPS ultimately attributed to the Client’s originating office.

Business Definition: NPS retained by a collecting or processing affiliate before intercompany remittance.
Business Context / Rule: Foreign NPS is the affiliate-retained component and does not form part of the final NPS earned by the Client Originating Office. It helps explain differences between NPS generated or retained across the royalty-processing chain and Client Office NPS. It should be analyzed separately from nps_am and in the Client Originating Office currency context exposed by the view.

Business Definition: An implementation indicator within Tempo’s Earnings Line Summarization layer that distinguishes affiliate and non-affiliate summarized populations.
Business Context / Rule: Client Financials intentionally includes only affiliate_income_ind = 'N'. Including both 'Y' and 'N' produces exactly double the expected values in every numerical measure when compared with the Tempo Client Financials screen. The approved reporting population for this view is therefore 'N' only. The detailed semantic intent of the source indicator remains a Tempo implementation detail and should not be inferred beyond this validated reporting rule.

Business Definition: A governed classification describing the royalty calculation basis applied to a calculated Client royalty receipt.
Business Context / Rule: Allowed values are At Source (1), Receipt (2), Limited Receipt (3), and Participant (4). Rate Type provides calculation context and can affect how royalty amounts are interpreted. Participant Rate Type is especially relevant because GL Posting Amount is expected to be zero for Participant earnings. Users should retain Rate Type when comparing calculations or investigating royalty outcomes.

Business Definition: The hierarchy of royalty-source attributes available for a calculated receipt: Source, Sub Source, Sub Sub Source, and Original Sub Sub Source.
Business Context / Rule: Client Financials exposes as much Source and Sub Source detail as is available in Tempo so users can trace royalty receipts to societies, affiliates, licensees, broadcasters, digital services, or other royalty providers. Hierarchy levels may be blank when Tempo has no lower-level source data. Source-country fields use one active country per Source, prioritizing the primary country and otherwise the most recently updated active country.

Business Definition: The selected active country associated with a Source hierarchy member.
Business Context / Rule: For each Source, the view selects one active Source Country. A country marked primary is preferred; if no primary country is available, the most recently updated active record is selected. The same rule is applied independently to Source, Sub Source, Sub Sub Source, and Original Sub Sub Source. Source Country is descriptive context and should not automatically be interpreted as the Client country or usage territory.

Business Definition: The association of a calculated Client royalty receipt with a specific Song and Song sequence in Tempo.
Business Context / Rule: Song-level detail is part of the validated Client Financials business grain. The view joins song_id and song_sequence_id to the current Song record to return the Song title. Users may aggregate above Song level, but should recognize that doing so removes detail visible in Tempo and may combine receipts that differ by Song, Contract, Source, Income Type, Rate Type, or other dimensions.

Business Definition: The control requiring financial measures returned by client_financials_v to equal the corresponding amounts displayed in the Tempo Client module Financial tab for equivalent filters and grouping.
Business Context / Rule: Reconciliation depends on using Statement Period reporting, Client Originating Office currency, and affiliate_income_ind = 'N'. Including both indicator populations doubles the measures. Differences should be investigated through filter alignment, currency, Song and Source detail, Contract context, Rate Type, Transaction Type, and completion of the Tempo Earnings Line Summarization process.

Business Definition: Governed reference data defining approved currency conversion factors, effective periods and uses.
Business Context / Rule: The two rate sets both convert local currency to USD but are not interchangeable because cadence, source and consuming process differ.

Business Definition: Quarter-end rate used by Tempo to convert Originating Office currency into USD.
Business Context / Rule: Select by Statement Period and Originating Office; use only for Tempo Intercompany Royalty Processing.

Business Definition: Tempo Statement Period for which an intercompany FX rate applies.
Business Context / Rule: Rate selection is Statement-Period based, not Accounting-Period based.

Business Definition: Treasury-provided month-end closing rate translating local currency to USD.
Business Context / Rule: Loaded monthly by Finance for Management Reporting and Month-End Close; not used by Tempo.

Business Definition: Month-end reporting period for which a closing rate applies.
Business Context / Rule: Use with Currency Code to select the approved closing rate.

Business Definition: Standard direction of both rate sets.
Business Context / Rule: Do not invert or treat as USD-to-local unless an approved reciprocal rule is explicitly applied.

Business Definition: Currency assigned to a Tempo Originating Office.
Business Context / Rule: Provides source-currency context for the intercompany rate.

Business Definition: Treasury-provided close position for a currency at month end.
Business Context / Rule: Used for Management Reporting and Month-End Close only.

Business Definition: Treasury supplies monthly closing rates used by Finance.
Business Context / Rule: Worldwide FP&A owns and stewards the monthly rate data; Finance performs the monthly load.

Business Definition: Update user and timestamp captured with monthly rates.
Business Context / Rule: Supports traceability of Finance loads and close investigations.

Business Definition: The current registration outcome reported by the recipient society for a submitted CWR registration.
Business Context / Rule:
Determine the current registration outcome using the Second Acknowledgement Status when available; otherwise use the First Acknowledgement Status. When no acknowledgement has been received, classify the registration as Pending.

ACK Status Codes represent the high-level outcome of recipient processing and should be interpreted together with associated Validation Messages, which provide the detailed technical reason for the outcome.

Map acknowledgement codes into enterprise reporting outcomes as follows:

Accepted: AC (Accepted With Changes), AS (Accepted As Sent), DU (Duplicate Registration)

No Participation: NP

Pending: RA (Registration Acknowledged), No Acknowledgement Received

Rejected: RC (Claim Rejected), RJ (Registration Rejected), XX (Legacy Manual Rejected Status)

Conflict: CO

Resolved Manually: RM (Registration Resolved Manually)

Unknown / Unconfirmed: DE, QU, 70, 80, 90, UP, and any unrecognized acknowledgement code.

Historical acknowledgement codes (70, 80, 90, UP, XX and other recipient-specific legacy values) should be retained for historical interpretation but may not represent currently active recipient processing outcomes.

Multiple-control registrations require additional interpretation because NP (No Participation) may represent an expected outcome for a specific territorial control group rather than a registration failure.
Related Assets / Fields: cwr_details_v; first_ack_status_cd; second_ack_status_cd; song_cwr_details_id; Reference Values: CWR Acknowledgement Status

Business Definition: The single registration-detail row selected to represent the current reporting outcome for a Song CWR Details ID and recipient when the CWR Details view contains multiple rows for that registration.
Business Context / Rule: Before counting or classifying registrations, reduce cwr_details_v to one authoritative row per song_cwr_details_id and recipient_cd. Prefer a row with a populated Second Acknowledgement Status Code. If multiple candidate rows remain, select the row with the latest Second Acknowledgement Date, followed by the latest First Acknowledgement Date, Update Date, and Create Date. Classifying the undeduplicated view can place the same registration in more than one status bucket and cause the sum of outcome counts to exceed submitted registrations.
Related Assets / Fields: cwr_details_v; song_cwr_details_id; recipient_cd; second_ack_status_cd; second_ack_dt; first_ack_dt; update_dt; create_dt

Business Definition: The sequence of distinct CWR registration attempts through which a Song is submitted, acknowledged, corrected, and potentially resubmitted to the same recipient.
Business Context / Rule: A registration attempt is identified by song_cwr_details_id. Multiple registration attempts may exist for the same song_id and recipient_cd. A later attempt is a distinct song_cwr_details_id for the same Song and recipient with a later CWR File Creation Date. For work-level analysis, Song Sequence ID should be retained for comparison but should not automatically prevent lifecycle matching unless sequence-specific registration behavior is confirmed.
Related Assets / Fields: cwr_details_v; song_id; song_sequence_id; song_cwr_details_id; recipient_cd; file_creation_dt

Business Definition: The operational classification describing whether a rejected, conflicted, or duplicate CWR registration was subsequently resubmitted to the same recipient and ultimately accepted.
Business Context / Rule: Compare an original exception registration to later registration attempts for the same song_id and recipient_cd, using a different song_cwr_details_id and a later File Creation Date. Classify as Resolved and Accepted when any later attempt has Final CWR Registration Status of Accepted. Classify as Re-sent, Not Yet Accepted when a later attempt exists but no later attempt is Accepted. Classify as No Subsequent Registration Found when no qualifying later attempt exists.
Related Assets / Fields: cwr_details_v; song_id; song_cwr_details_id; recipient_cd; file_creation_dt; first_ack_status_cd; second_ack_status_cd

Business Definition: The elapsed number of calendar days between the original exception registration file and the later registration file selected as the resolving or most relevant subsequent attempt.
Business Context / Rule: Calculate as the difference in days between the original File Creation Date and the subsequent File Creation Date. When an accepted subsequent registration exists, use the earliest later accepted attempt. When no accepted attempt exists but the registration was resubmitted, use the most recent later attempt for current-status investigation. Leave the duration null when no subsequent registration is found. File Creation Date may not provide reliable ordering for multiple attempts created on the same date.

Business Definition: A musical work whose ownership or administration differs by territory, requiring separate territorial control-group representations within the CWR registration process.
Business Context / Rule:
Multiple Controls processing exists because the CWR standard supports territory-specific ownership, collection rights, and administration structures through territorial control records and inclusion/exclusion territory definitions. Different territorial control groups may therefore be represented as separate registration submissions.

Expected recipient responses may vary by territorial control group. A No Participation (NP) acknowledgement may represent an expected outcome for a non-applicable territorial control group rather than a registration failure.

Registration reporting should consider territorial control context before classifying NP acknowledgements as unsuccessful registrations.

Business Definition: A structured validation message returned by a recipient through a CWR MSG record during acknowledgement processing. The message identifies the record type being validated, severity level, validation rule, and explanatory text describing why an acknowledgement outcome occurred.
Business Context / Rule:
WR Validation Messages should be interpreted together with the associated ACK Status Code.

The ACK Status identifies the outcome of recipient processing (Accepted, Rejected, Conflict, No Participation, etc.), while the Validation Message explains the reason for that outcome.

Validation Messages are derived from CWR MSG records and typically contain:
<Record Type>
<Message Severity>
<Validation Number>
<Message Text>

In Tempo, MSG components are stored as a concatenated string within: song_ack_message_tx and therefore require parsing to expose the underlying structure.

Validation Messages are authoritative for troubleshooting, recipient-specific issue identification, root-cause analysis, and registration-quality investigations.
